name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 342 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 342 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: India raised its fiscal-year growth forecast while security forces in Chhattisgarh uncovered a major Maoist weapons cache, recovering two IEDs. In Kashmir, LG Manoj Sinha chaired meetings, ordered a crackdown on terror modules and tighter counter-infiltration grids, and the Mirwaiz called for the release of political prisoners and restoration of civil liberties. In Manipur, a district shutdown began after two Kuki youths went missing, the state announced ex-gratia for families of 32 Kuki-Zo civilians killed, and it seeks relaxed permit norms for Indian-origin tourists. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: India hevet sin vekstprognose for regnskapsåret, mens sikkerhetsstyrker i Chhattisgarh avdekket en stor maoistisk våpenlager og gjenvant to IED-er. I Kashmir ledet LG Manoj Sinha møter, beordret en nedslag på terrormoduler og strengere motinfiltrasjonsnett, og Mirwaiz oppfordret til løslatelse av politiske fanger og gjenoppretting av sivile friheter. I Manipur startet en distriktsnedstengning etter at to Kuki-ungdommer forsvant, staten kunngjorde eks-gratia til familiene til 32 Kuki-Zo-sivile som ble drept, og den søker lempede tillatelsesregler for turister med indisk opprinnelse. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
